$comment: X-20 NORMATIVE LINT CATALOGUE (single source of truth). Each rule is a faithful transcription of the reference conformance tool that implements it; scripts/*.py are the versioned REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION of this catalogue. docs/lint-catalogue.md is generated from this file by scripts/lint_catalogue.py; tests/test_lint_catalogue.py enforces completeness (every emitted rule is catalogued), no phantom entries, and test traceability. `non_rule_tokens` lists LINT-shaped strings in the sources that are prefixes/placeholders, NOT rules.

non_rule_tokens.LINT-BND-I: R5-02: the PREFIX that classifies a verdict, not a rule id. `is_incomplete()` tests `rule.startswith('LINT-BND-I')` to separate INCOMPLETE from violation and from advisory warning, exactly as `is_warning()` tests the W prefix. The rules themselves are catalogued individually (LINT-BND-I1).
non_rule_tokens.LINT-BND-W: prefix used by bundle_lint startswith() to split warnings from violations; the rule is LINT-BND-W1
non_rule_tokens.LINT-DISC-NN: docstring placeholder ('stable LINT-DISC-NN rule ids'), not a rule
non_rule_tokens.LINT-DISC-P: prefix of the LINT-DISC-P-* family used in prose
non_rule_tokens.LINT-MAN-03: retired 2026-09-27 and named in the docstring of `lint_manifest`, which explains why it no longer exists; never emitted. Recorded in `retired` with the reason — the identifier is not reused
non_rule_tokens.LINT-PKG-04: historical cross-reference in a comment (sign-then-timestamp verification); never emitted — a numbering gap
non_rule_tokens.LINT-PROD: prefix of the LINT-PROD-* family used in prose
non_rule_tokens.LINT-RLY: prefix of the LINT-RLY-* family used in prose
non_rule_tokens.LINT-TRUST: prefix of the LINT-TRUST-* family used in prose

retired.$comment: Rules withdrawn from the profile. An identifier is assigned ONCE and is never reused, so a rule that leaves the catalogue is recorded here with the reason rather than deleted: a reader of an artefact sealed under an earlier edition, or of a checker built from an earlier catalogue, can still find out what the identifier meant and why it is gone.

was.precondition: a manifest part carries a nested `manifest` AND depth >= 1
was.predicate: Manifest nesting depth MUST NOT exceed 1.

LINT-MAN-03.reason: Unreachable by construction, and the rule it guarded was never the profile's rule. A part descriptor admits no `manifest` member in the Schema (additionalProperties: false) or in the CDDL, so a nested manifest is not expressible; and a part's `digest` is in the observed-octets domain, which admits no manifest mode, so a digest committing to a nested structure has no representation either. The prose permitted 'nesting at most one level', which described neither authority; it was corrected to state that a manifest is flat, and this rule went with it. It was filed under coverage_gap for its whole life, which recorded the symptom without asking why.

rules.input: any evidence object (top-level or an EP outcome/change)
rules.precondition: always — runs on every object dispatched through lint_object
rules.predicate: The object's `type` MUST be one of {SE-v1, DE-v1, NDE-v1, RE-v1, CE-v1, EP-v1, RelayEvidence-v1}; any other or missing type fails.
rules.error: unknown or missing evidence type: {t!r}

rules.precondition: type == SE-v1
rules.predicate: se.auth_context.method (a missing auth_context treated as {}) MUST equal se.auth_method.
rules.error: SE auth_context.method != auth_method

rules.precondition: type == DE-v1
rules.predicate: de.auth_context.method (missing auth_context treated as {}) MUST equal de.recipient_auth_method.
rules.error: DE auth_context.method != recipient_auth_method

rules.input: evidence object carrying an auth_context (SE, DE, RE, GCM)
rules.precondition: auth_context.method is REGISTERED in registries/auth-assurance.json
rules.predicate: The (identity, method, loa) tuple MUST be admissible — (a) the registered method's own admissible_loa set bounds what it can truthfully claim (no scalar ordering: password-otp never claims high, mls-x509 never very-high); (b) the evidence context's tuple row bounds the combination: se-submission split by origin_proof, de-confirmation split by wallet-signed vs session, de-availability, re-member-refusal, gcm-dispute — with combined-factor ELEVATION stated where a wallet signature admits a substantial session that the session-only/provider-attested arm does not. The floors are the pilot profile's provisional set; their legal adoption is TODO(legal) and left open. Fail-closed.
rules.error: a registered method claiming a loa outside its admissible set, or an (identity, method, loa) tuple outside the evidence context's admissible row (X-27)

rules.precondition: auth_context.method is a non-empty string NOT registered in registries/auth-assurance.json
rules.predicate: The safe-generic-processing convention: an UNREGISTERED well-formed method is accepted, preserved verbatim, and treated as UNASSESSED — a WARNING, not a violation. Registering the method (with its admissible loa set) in registries/auth-assurance.json is a registry action.
rules.error: auth method is not registered — the assurance claim is unassessed (warning)

rules.precondition: always (any bundle)
rules.predicate: The MED MUST declare scope support (mls.scopes_supported truthy) if and only if the ORG publishes a scope_map object.
rules.error: MED scopes_supported={s} but ORG scope_map present={h}

rules.precondition: per scope, per role in scope.roles
rules.predicate: Every role of every scope MUST be held by at least one active member (status=='active' whose roles include the role).
rules.error: scope {sid!r} role {role!r} is held by no active member

rules.input: ORG scope roles + BW-MEMBER device capabilities
rules.precondition: role has >=1 active holder / scope has role holders
rules.predicate: A role with active holders MUST have at least one holder with a 'receive'-capable device; and each scope's members MUST include at least one 'ack'-capable device (else acceptance is impossible).
rules.error: scope {sid!r} role {role!r}: no active member device can 'receive' | scope {sid!r}: no member device can 'ack' (acceptance impossible)

rules.precondition: scope.acceptance_policy_ref present / evidence addressed to this entity with a dict acceptance_policy_ref
rules.predicate: A scope's acceptance_policy_ref MUST be a key of org.acceptance_policy; and an evidence acceptance_policy_ref.policy_version MUST equal org.policy_version.
rules.error: scope {sid!r} acceptance_policy_ref {apr!r} is not an acceptance_policy key | {type} acceptance_policy_ref.policy_version {a!r} != ORG policy_version {b!r}

rules.input: evidence scope_ref vs ORG scope map
rules.precondition: evidence addressed to this entity AND ev.scope_ref is a dict
rules.predicate: If scope_ref.scope_id == 'default', version MUST == '1'; otherwise some ORG scope MUST have both scope_id and version equal to the reference.
rules.error: {type} scope_ref default/{v!r} — the implicit default scope is fixed at descriptor version '1' (§8.3a) | {type} scope_ref {sid!r}/{v!r} does not resolve against the ORG scope map

rules.input: bundle: MED, ORG and every MEMBER vs manifest entity_uid
rules.precondition: always (any bundle)
rules.predicate: For each named document (MED, ORG, each MEMBER), doc.uid MUST equal the bundle's entity_uid.
rules.error: {name} uid {a!r} != bundle entity {b!r}

rules.input: ORG acceptance_policy entries and scope-referenced policy strings
rules.precondition: per acceptance_policy value; per top-level policy key not naming an org role
rules.predicate: Each policy MUST match ^(any-one|all|quorum:(\d+)|device-class:.+)$; a 'quorum:n' with n<1 is malformed.
rules.error: {ctx}: acceptance_policy {name!r} = {pol!r} is not any-one|all|quorum:<n>|device-class:<class> | {ctx}: {pol!r} is malformed (quorum n must be >= 1) | acceptance_policy[{key!r}] = {pol!r} is not any-one|all|quorum:<n>|device-class:<class>

rules.input: acceptance policy 'any-one'/'quorum:n' + eligible active ack-capable members
rules.precondition: policy matches grammar and is any-one or quorum:n
rules.predicate: Let ackers = distinct-by-mid eligible members holding an ack-capable device. For 'quorum:n', len(ackers) MUST be >= n; for 'any-one', ackers MUST be non-empty.
rules.error: {ctx}: {pol!r} unsatisfiable — {k} distinct active, ack-capable member(s) eligible, {n} required | {ctx}: 'any-one' unsatisfiable — no active, ack-capable member is eligible

rules.precondition: policy == 'all'
rules.predicate: The eligible set (distinct-by-mid) MUST be non-empty AND every distinct member MUST hold an ack-capable device.
rules.error: {ctx}: 'all' over an empty eligible set is ambiguous — rejected | {ctx}: 'all' unreachable — eligible member(s) {lacking} have no ack-capable device

rules.input: evidence acceptance_policy_ref.doc_digest vs ORG signed payload
rules.precondition: evidence addressed to this entity; acceptance_policy_ref.policy_version == org.policy_version
rules.predicate: doc_digest.hex MUST equal SHA-256 hex of dcbor(ORG minus doc_cose_b64) AND doc_digest.hash_mode MUST == 'raw-sha256'.
rules.error: {type} acceptance_policy_ref.doc_digest does not match the ORG signed payload (raw-SHA-256 …, hash_mode raw-sha256) — §8.3

rules.input: availability-grade evidence + ORG delivery_grades (+ optional grade-reveal fixture)
rules.precondition: evidence addressed to this entity; delivery_grade == 'availability'
rules.predicate: With a reveal for the message_id: grade_commitment MUST == compute_grade_commitment(salt, content_class, org_digest) AND delivery_grades[content_class] MUST == 'availability'. Without a reveal: 'availability' MUST appear among delivery_grades values.
rules.error: {type} grade_commitment does not match the reveal … | revealed content class {cc!r} is not declared availability-grade … (availability is never implicit) | {type} is availability-grade but ORG declares no availability-grade content class

rules.input: evidence recipient confirmation + quorum ackers vs BW-MEMBER roster
rules.precondition: evidence addressed to this entity; confirmation/quorum entries carry a mid
rules.predicate: The confirmation's mid (and device_id when present) and every quorum acker mid MUST resolve to an active member of this entity that is ack-capable (the named device enrolled with 'ack', or any ack-capable device when no device_id). Evidence 2.3: a wallet-signed quorum entry names its device — the (mid, device_id) pair is resolved; a provider entry resolves the member alone. The member and device are resolved AS OF THE ACT (the confirmation's own instant), not from the current-status map — a confirmation valid when it was made does not become unresolvable when the member later retires, and a member who was NOT active at the act still fails. Where no version history is supplied the bundle's single current version is used and the behaviour is unchanged.
rules.error: {type} confirmation mid {mid!r} does not resolve to an active, ack-capable member of {entity!r} ({why}) — TS clause 6 INTF-2 | {type} quorum acker {mid!r} does not resolve … INTF-2

rules.input: the whole evidence set (message_id, recipient_uid, payload_hash)
rules.precondition: an evidence object has a message_id already seen on another object
rules.predicate: For a repeated message_id, the recipient_uid MUST agree and the payload_hash MUST agree across all objects sharing it (global message_id uniqueness per issuing environment, S4).
rules.error: message_id {mid!r} maps to two recipients ({a!r}, {b!r}) — must be globally unique (S4) | message_id {mid!r} maps to two payload_hash values — must be globally unique (S4)

rules.precondition: auth_context.identity == 'system' and the acting mid resolves in this entity's roster
rules.predicate: The resolved acting member MUST have status=='active' AND member_type=='system'.
rules.error: {type} auth_context.identity=system names mid {amid!r}, not an active system member of {entity!r} (status={s!r}, member_type={t!r}) — Annex R (A1)

rules.input: SE mandate_ref vs the acting system member's standing mandate (+ optional mandate-reveal fixture)
rules.precondition: auth_context.identity=='system'; type=='SE-v1'; mandate_ref is a dict; acting member resolves
rules.predicate: mandate_ref issuer/id MUST match the standing mandate; when sent_at is present it MUST lie in the standing validity window; with a reveal, the mandate_commitment MUST match compute_mandate_commitment(salt, id, content_class, doc_digest) AND the revealed content_class MUST be in the standing mandate scope.
rules.error: SE mandate_ref (issuer/id) does not match the standing mandate of {amid!r} (A2) | SE acted under mandate {id!r} outside its validity window at sent_at {t!r} (A2) | SE mandate_commitment does not match the reveal … | revealed content class {cc!r} is not in the mandate scope of {amid!r} — agent overreach (A1)

rules.input: human_acceptance ORG scope + its eligible active members
rules.precondition: scope.acceptance_policy_ref is a policy key; scope.human_acceptance truthy; eligible set non-empty
rules.predicate: At least one eligible member MUST be a human (member_type != 'system') — a human-gated policy MUST NOT be unsatisfiable by agents alone.
rules.error: scope {sid!r} is human_acceptance but every eligible member is a system member (Annex R, A3)

rules.precondition: scope.recoverability=='records' and records_role set
rules.predicate: The records_role MUST be held by at least one active member (so the records leaf resolves).
rules.error: scope {sid!r} is recoverability=records but its records_role {rr!r} is held by no active member (§8.3a, F16)

rules.input: evidence acknowledgement on a human_acceptance scope vs roster
rules.precondition: evidence addressed to this entity; scope_ref resolves to a scope with human_acceptance
rules.predicate: No acking mid (the confirmation's mid or any quorum acker) may resolve to an active system member — agents may verify S3 but not legally accept S4 a human-gated class. The member's standing is resolved AT THE ACT, not from the current roster. The act-time resolver was added BESIDE this gate rather than replacing it, so the gate went on deciding attribution from today's membership. At THIS rule the current-state read failed OPEN: a member who had since retired was absent from the map, so a SYSTEM member's acknowledgement in a human_acceptance scope was never checked at all.
rules.error: {type} acknowledgement by system member {amid!r} does not satisfy the human_acceptance scope {sid!r} (Annex R, A8, §8.3)

rules.input: RelayEvidence B.2-RelayRejection + the sender-facing NDE for the same message_id
rules.precondition: RelayEvidence-v1 event=='B.2-RelayRejection'; an NDE exists for the message_id; the reason has a mapping
rules.predicate: The paired NDE's reason MUST equal RELAY_B2_TO_NDE[relay.reason] (the typed relay-rejection reason maps to the correct sender-facing NDE reason).
rules.error: B.2 RelayRejection reason {r!r} for message {mid!r} maps to sender NDE reason {expected!r}, but the NDE carries {actual!r} — TS clause 4.1

rules.input: EP rdp_chain[i].evidence reference + the referenced RelayEvidence object in the bundle
rules.precondition: type=='EP-v1'; the hop evidence resolves to a RelayEvidence-v1 present in the bundle
rules.predicate: hop.evidence.seal_digest.hex MUST equal compute_seal_digest(target.seal.cose_b64) = SHA-256 over the DECODED COSE_Sign1 bytes (not the base64 text).
rules.error: EP rdp_chain[{i}].evidence.seal_digest.hex {a!r} does not match the referenced object's seal: expected {b!r} = SHA-256 over the DECODED COSE_Sign1 bytes (TS clause 4.1)

rules.input: EVERY wallet-signed recipient-side proof (recipient_confirmation, recipient_validation_failure, s3_attestation) + the device's published confirmation_key anchor
rules.precondition: evidence addressed to this entity; any recipient-side proof field carries wallet_signature_b64 OR a quorum entry has attestation == 'wallet-signed'
rules.predicate: The confirmation MUST carry a device_id; (mid, device_id) MUST resolve to a device with a confirmation_key.public_key_b64; and the wallet signature MUST verify against that key under the algorithm the anchor DECLARES — EdDSA, ES256 or ES384, with THREE-WAY AGREEMENT between the COSE protected `alg`, the published `confirmation_key.alg` and the key's actual type/curve (one encoding per algorithm, I-D Confirmation-key encodings). This predicate said 'Ed25519' after the verifier became algorithm-neutral, and the generated catalogue is NORMATIVE — an assessor could reject a conforming EC confirmation on it. Fail-closed. Evidence 2.3 extends the same check to wallet-signed quorum entries: each is an independently portable per-member proof, resolved per (mid, device_id) and verified against that member's published anchor. R27-PUB-02: the check runs ONCE PER selected proof field. It used to run after the loop that selects them, on whichever field was iterated last — `s3_attestation` — so a forged recipient_confirmation or recipient_validation_failure on evidence carrying no s3 attestation was never verified at all.
rules.error: {type} {field} by {mid!r} is wallet-signed but carries no device_id (finding D) | {type} {field} by {mid!r}/{did!r} has no resolvable confirmation_key anchor (finding D) | {type} {field} wallet_signature_b64 does not verify against the published confirmation key of {mid!r}/{did!r} (INTF-1/S1)

rules.input: SE expires_at + the DE/NDE outcome for the same message_id (or an EP's se + outcomes)
rules.precondition: an SE with expires_at exists for the outcome's message_id; outcome type is DE-v1 or NDE-v1
rules.predicate: An NDE with reason=='expired' MUST have observed_at >= expires_at (no premature expiry); a DE at EVERY grade — availability INCLUDED (the former exemption is removed) — MUST have delivered_at <= expires_at, where delivered_at is the S2/S4 EVENT time (the artefact's qualified timestamp is the possibly-later issuance time). A tie (delivered_at == expires_at) is delivered.
rules.error: NDE `expired` for {mid!r} observed at {obs} BEFORE SE.expires_at {exp} — premature expiry (R1) | {grade}-grade DE for {mid!r} delivered at {d} AFTER SE.expires_at {exp} — delivery past the authenticated deadline (R1/X-21; the event time bounds every grade, availability included)

rules.precondition: always (any bundle)
rules.predicate: MID non-reuse: within the bundle's UID, no MID may be bound to two BW-MEMBER documents carrying different accountability.authorisation_ref values. A MID is a permanent attribution key in indefinitely-retained evidence; reassigning it to a different member/authorisation chain would silently re-attribute old confirmations. Checked across ALL members (any status), which also surfaces the duplicate-MID case the active-member map would otherwise silently collapse.
rules.error: MID {mid!r} is bound to two different accountability.authorisation_ref ({a!r} and {b!r}) — a MID MUST NOT be reassigned to a different member/authorisation chain within a UID (X-17)

rules.precondition: always (any bundle); evaluated for each evidence object (and each EP's embedded se) carrying a recipient_addr
rules.predicate: Address resolution: a recipient_addr MUST be a well-formed bw: address (umbrella Annex A). When it is addressed to this bundle's entity, a role address (.../r/<role>) MUST name a declared role of the entity's BW-ORG (its roles[], acceptance_policy keys, or any scope roles/records_role), and a member address (.../u/<MID>) MUST name a published member — so every address resolves. (Schema tightening already guarantees the converse: every declared role is addressable.). The address's UID MUST equal the UID of the object it addresses. This was a bare `continue` commented "addressed to a different entity — not this bundle's org" — true, irrelevant, and exactly wrong: the object is THIS bundle's evidence addressed to THIS entity, so a foreign UID is the defect, not someone else's business. Selection read only the /r/<role> tail, so an address naming another entity selected a role out of this entity's acceptance_policy map.
rules.error: {type} recipient_addr {addr!r} is not a well-formed bw: address (X-16) | {type} recipient_addr names role {role!r}, not a declared role of {entity!r} — an address MUST resolve to a declared role (X-16) | {type} recipient_addr names member {mid!r}, not a published member of {entity!r} (X-16)

rules.input: bundle manifest (RelayEvidence hops vs the SE / EP-embedded SE)
rules.precondition: a RelayEvidence-v1 in the bundle shares its message_id with an SE (standalone or EP-embedded) carrying envelope_hash
rules.predicate: Evidence 2.2: a relay hop's envelope_hash MUST equal the SE's for the same message_id — each hop attests the exact TLS-serialized MLSMessage octets it handled, so a substituted ciphertext under unchanged metadata fails at every hop.
rules.error: relay hop for {message_id!r} attests a different envelope_hash than the SE — substituted ciphertext under the same metadata (F-02)

rules.input: bundle manifest (GCM-v1 objects, standalone or EP disputes[], vs the ORG and the sealed SE/DE)
rules.precondition: a GCM-v1 in the bundle is pinned to THIS bundle's ORG policy_version and carries a reveal
rules.predicate: Evidence 2.7, rewritten: a grade-mismatch dispute is valid only when BOTH (a) PROOF OF ATTRIBUTION holds — the reveal_confirmation verifies against the disputing device's published confirmation_key as of read_at (INTF-1/1a/2) and its signed tuple (message_id, envelope_hash, grade_commitment, salt, content_class, read_at, recipient_uid, mid) matches the disputed evidence — AND (b) MISMATCH holds — the recomputation differs from the sealed commitment, or it matches but the revealed class is not availability-declared. The former rule accepted (b) alone; inequality is manufacturable by inventing a salt, so any recipient provider could rebut any availability-grade DE. Malformed commitment input yields a TYPED violation, never an uncaught exception in the validator. Scope: (a) proves an attributable assertion, not objective extraction from the ciphertext. The member's standing is resolved AT THE ACT, not from the current roster. The act-time resolver was added BESIDE this gate rather than replacing it, so the gate went on deciding attribution from today's membership.
rules.error: dispute without a verifying recipient confirmation, a signed tuple not covering the disputed values, malformed commitment input, or a void (matching + availability-declared) reveal (DR-03)

rules.input: bundle manifest (SEs addressed to this entity vs the ORG max_ttl)
rules.precondition: an SE (standalone or EP-embedded) addressed to this entity carries sent_at and expires_at in order
rules.predicate: The TTL (expires_at - sent_at) MUST NOT exceed the recipient's declared maximum — BW-ORG.max_ttl (ISO 8601 duration, days/time designators), absent = the profile default P30D.
rules.error: SE for {message_id!r} carries a TTL of {ttl} — beyond the recipient's maximum {max_ttl} (X-22: expires_at is validated against policy, not echoed)

rules.input: assembled bundle (entity, med, org, members, evidence)
rules.precondition: an evidence object has type == SE-v1 AND sender_uid == entity_uid AND sender_confirmation is present
rules.predicate: D4 (evidence 2.3): the sender-side mirror of LINT-BND-21 (INTF-1b). The sender_confirmation's mid MUST resolve to an ACTIVE member of the sender entity, and its wallet signature MUST verify against that member's published confirmation_key anchor per (mid, device_id) — so a provider cannot mint 'the sender authorised these bytes' under its own key. Fail-closed on unknown mid, no resolvable anchor, or a non-verifying signature. The member's standing is resolved AT THE ACT, not from the current roster. The act-time resolver was added BESIDE this gate rather than replacing it, so the gate went on deciding attribution from today's membership.
rules.error: sender_confirmation mid unknown to the sender entity, no (mid, device_id) anchor, or a signature that does not verify against the published confirmation key (X-03/D4)

rules.input: assembled recipient bundle (entity, med, org, members, evidence)
rules.precondition: an evidence object has type == RE-v1 AND refusal_kind == 'member'
rules.predicate: Evidence 2.3: a member refusal is an attributable act. The refusing mid MUST resolve to an ACTIVE member of the recipient entity (no ack capability required — declining is not acknowledging), and a wallet-signed refusal_confirmation MUST verify against the member's published confirmation_key anchor resolved per (mid, device_id) from BW-MEMBER — the same finding-D machinery as an acceptance, so a provider cannot mint 'the user refused' under its own key. Fail-closed on no device_id, no resolvable anchor, or a non-verifying signature. The member's standing is resolved AT THE ACT, not from the current roster. The act-time resolver was added BESIDE this gate rather than replacing it, so the gate went on deciding attribution from today's membership.
rules.error: refusing mid unknown/inactive, no (mid, device_id) anchor, or a refusal_confirmation signature that does not verify against the published confirmation key (X-29)

rules.input: assembled bundle (entity, med, org, members, evidence)
rules.precondition: an evidence object's acceptance_policy_ref.doc_digest pins THIS bundle's BW-ORG
rules.predicate: Evidence 2.4: the evidence names the EXACT policy selected, recomputably. (a) acceptance_policy_ref.policy_key MUST exist in the pinned ORG's acceptance_policy map; (b) where the message's SE is available (in the bundle, or the enclosing EP's), policy_key MUST equal the deterministic umbrella §8.3 selection recomputed from the SE's (scope_ref, recipient_addr) and the ORG (lint_cli.select_policy_key — scoped: the scope's acceptance_policy_ref key; default-scope role-addressed: the role's key else 'default'; entity-addressed: 'default'); (c) a DE carrying acceptance_policy_kind MUST carry the kind of acceptance_policy[policy_key]. Two keys in one BW-ORG can never produce indistinguishable evidence. The recomputation FAILS CLOSED where the SE carries no `recipient_addr` — absence used to resolve to 'default' exactly as an explicit entity address did, so the recomputation confirmed a downgrade rather than catching it (it used the same stripped input).
rules.error: policy_key unknown to the pinned ORG, differing from the recomputed selection, or a DE kind differing from the keyed policy (F-08)

rules.input: assembled bundle (entity, med, org, members, evidence)
rules.precondition: a B.2-RelayRejection RelayEvidence and the sender-side NDE for the same message_id are both in the bundle
rules.predicate: The translated NDE is a RELAY-stage outcome — it follows the sender-side A.1 SubmissionAcceptance, so its event MUST be B.3-RelayFailure. An A.2-SubmissionRejection here makes the EP's timeline read as accepted-then-rejected-BEFORE-submission — chronologically invalid when the EP is read alone. Complements LINT-BND-19 (which binds the reasons); the mapping is the TS clause 4.1 table, documented as a translation pending standards-owner (ETSI TC ESI) review.
rules.error: sender NDE translating a B.2 RelayRejection carries a non-relay-stage event (X-28)

rules.input: assembled bundle (entity, med, org, members, evidence)
rules.precondition: two device records anywhere in the member set carry a confirmation_key
rules.predicate: Confirmation-key uniqueness across the whole member set — the same public key on two (mid, device_id) records, across devices, members or entities, makes a signature resolve to more than one device and security class; device-bound assurance collapses. Fail-closed.
rules.error: a confirmation key shared by two device records in the bundle (X-32)

rules.input: assembled bundle (entity, med, org, members, evidence)
rules.precondition: an evidence object's acceptance_policy_ref.doc_digest pins THIS bundle's BW-ORG, and the governing SE carries sent_at
rules.predicate: The pinned version was IN FORCE at the act. (a) BW-ORG.valid_from <= SE.sent_at; (b) for a scoped message, the matched scope_map entry's valid_from <= SE.sent_at (a scope can be introduced into an already-in-force ORG, so the arms are independent). Deterministic selection and a recomputable selected key did not, by themselves, bound the version in TIME, so evidence could be evaluated under rules that did not yet exist when the act took place. Parsed instants; a tie (valid_from == sent_at) is in force.
rules.error: evidence pins a BW-ORG in force from {vf} for a message sent at {sent} | evidence is scoped to {sid} v{ver} in force from {svf} for a message sent at {sent} (DR-04, umbrella §8.3)

rules.input: assembled bundle, plus (optional) a per-MID BW-MEMBER version history and the ROSTER-v1 snapshot covering the evidence epoch
rules.precondition: a confirmation names (mid, device_id) — sender, s3/acceptance, wallet-signed quorum entry, member refusal, or GCM reveal
rules.predicate: The member version AND the device key are resolved AS THEY STOOD AT THE ACT (sent_at / verified_at / read_at / refused_at per object), not as they stand now. (a) exactly ONE history version is in force at the act — overlapping windows, a history that does not cover the act, and unparsable bounds are REJECTED rather than resolved by manifest order; (b) where a ROSTER-v1 snapshot covers the epoch, the selected version's digest MUST equal the snapshot's member_doc_digest; (c) device.added_at <= act_time and any removal boundary is honoured, so a key minted after the fact cannot anchor an earlier act. rules.precondition: type not in {BW-MED-v1, BW-ORG-v1, BW-MEMBER-v1}
rules.predicate: doc.type MUST equal one of the three recognised discovery types; otherwise the linter returns immediately with no further checks.
rules.error: not a discovery document: {t!r}

rules.precondition: always (the doc_cose_b64 field is examined)
rules.predicate: doc.doc_cose_b64 MUST be valid Base64, decode to a 4-element COSE_Sign1 array, and its embedded payload (cose[2]) MUST byte-equal dcbor(doc minus the doc_cose_b64 key).
rules.error: doc_cose_b64 is not valid Base64 | doc_cose_b64 does not decode to CBOR | doc_cose_b64 is not a 4-element COSE_Sign1 array | doc_cose_b64 payload does not match the canonical document (stale/tampered)

rules.precondition: doc_cose_b64 decodes to a 4-element COSE_Sign1 (cbor2 available)
rules.predicate: The COSE_Sign1 protected-header alg (label 1) MUST be in the allowlist {-8, -7, -35}.
rules.error: doc_cose_b64 COSE alg {alg!r} not in the allowlist

rules.precondition: always
rules.predicate: doc.uid MUST be a well-formed EU UID (UID_RE = ^EU-[A-Z]{2}-(EOID|PSBID)-[0-9A-HJ-NP-TV-Z]{14}$) AND its two check characters C1 C2 MUST verify as the GF(2^5) Reed-Solomon check symbols (umbrella Annex F). A checksum-invalid UID is rejected.
rules.error: uid is not a well-formed EU UID: {uid!r} | uid {uid!r} has an invalid check symbol (C1C2) — the GF(2^5) Reed-Solomon check does not verify

rules.precondition: type == BW-ORG-v1
rules.predicate: policy_version and valid_from MUST be present; acceptance_policy MUST be a non-empty object; every value MUST match ^(any-one|all|quorum:\d+|device-class:.+)$.
rules.error: BW-ORG must carry policy_version | BW-ORG must carry valid_from | BW-ORG acceptance_policy must be a non-empty object | BW-ORG acceptance_policy[{role!r}] is not a valid policy: {pol!r}

rules.precondition: type == BW-MED-v1
rules.predicate: mls.cipher_suites MUST be a non-empty list; rdp.keypackage_url and rdp.ds_url MUST be https URLs; expires_at MUST be present; mls.scopes_supported, if present, MUST be boolean.
rules.error: BW-MED mls.cipher_suites must be a non-empty list | BW-MED mls.{url_field} must be an https URL | BW-MED must declare expires_at (freshness bound) | BW-MED mls.scopes_supported must be a boolean when present

rules.precondition: type == BW-MEMBER-v1
rules.predicate: doc.mid MUST match MID_RE (^[0-9A-HJ-NP-TV-Z]{9}$) AND its 9th character MUST verify as the GF(2^5) Reed-Solomon check symbol of the 8 payload symbols; devices MUST be a non-empty list; every device MUST contain mls_leaf_node_ref.
rules.error: BW-MEMBER mid is not a well-formed MID: {mid!r} | BW-MEMBER mid {mid!r} has an invalid check symbol — the GF(2^5) Reed-Solomon check does not verify | BW-MEMBER must list at least one device | BW-MEMBER devices[{i}] missing mls_leaf_node_ref

rules.precondition: doc_cose_b64 decodes to a 4-element COSE_Sign1 (cbor2 available)
rules.predicate: The COSE payload element (cose[2]) MUST be an embedded byte string, not detached.
rules.error: doc_cose_b64 COSE payload is detached (not embedded)

rules.precondition: scope_map present
rules.predicate: scope_map.scopes MUST be a non-empty list of objects; each scope MUST contain scope_id, version, valid_from, roles, content_classes, recoverability, acceptance_policy_ref; recoverability MUST be in {strict, records}.
rules.error: scope_map.scopes must be a non-empty list | scope_map.scopes[{i}] is not an object | scope_map.scopes[{i}] missing {f} | scope_map.scopes[{i}] recoverability {r!r} not in {strict, records}

rules.precondition: scope_map present
rules.predicate: Any present fallback (per-scope scope.fallback or map-level scope_map.fallback) MUST equal 'default'.
rules.error: scope_map.scopes[{i}] fallback must be 'default' when present | scope_map.fallback must be 'default' when present

rules.precondition: scope_map present
rules.predicate: The scope_id values across scope_map.scopes MUST be unique.
rules.error: scope_map has a duplicate scope_id {sid!r}

rules.precondition: scope_map present
rules.predicate: Each content_class MUST route to at most one scope (it must not appear in two scopes with different scope_ids).
rules.error: content_class {cc!r} maps to more than one scope ({a!r} and {b!r})

rules.precondition: scope_map present
rules.predicate: For each scope, a non-null acceptance_policy_ref MUST be a key present in doc.acceptance_policy.
rules.error: scope_map.scopes[{i}] acceptance_policy_ref {apr!r} is not an acceptance_policy key

rules.precondition: scope_map present
rules.predicate: Every role listed in a scope's roles MUST exist in the organisation-level roles (doc.roles).
rules.error: scope_map.scopes[{i}] role {r!r} is not an organisation-level role

rules.precondition: scope_map present
rules.predicate: No scope may declare scope_id == 'default' (that id is reserved for the implicit scope).
rules.error: scope_map.scopes[{i}] scope_id 'default' is reserved (implicit scope)

rules.precondition: --verify-demo mode; cbor2 available and doc_cose_b64 valid
rules.predicate: The seal's COSE kid MUST equal 'entity-admin' AND the Ed25519 signature MUST verify against the published entity-admin demo key.
rules.error: discovery doc sealed with kid {kid!r}, expected 'entity-admin' (entity wallet-administration signer) | discovery seal signature does not verify against the entity-admin demo key

rules.precondition: scope_map present; per content_class within each scope
rules.predicate: Each content_class in a scope MUST match CONTENT_CLASS_RE (lowercase-kebab, optionally x- prefixed with a non-empty name); a non-x- class MUST be a TIER-1 class REGISTERED in registries/content-classes.json (the tier-1 set is loaded from the machine-readable registry artefact, umbrella §13.4 — promoting a class is a registry action, not a lint-code release). Private classes MUST carry the x- prefix.
rules.error: scope_map.scopes[{i}] content_class {cc!r} is not lowercase-kebab (optionally x- prefixed) | scope_map.scopes[{i}] content_class {cc!r} is neither a standard registry class nor x- prefixed

rules.precondition: delivery_grades present
rules.predicate: delivery_grades MUST be a non-empty object; each key MUST be a well-formed content class; each value MUST be in {availability, verification, acceptance}.
rules.error: delivery_grades must be a non-empty object | delivery_grades key {cls!r} is not a well-formed content class | delivery_grades[{cls!r}] = {g!r} not in {availability, verification, acceptance}

rules.precondition: delivery_grades present; per scope whose acceptance_policy_ref resolves to a policy
rules.predicate: For each scope, the implied grade is 'acceptance' if its policy == 'all' or starts 'quorum:', else 'verification'; every content_class in that scope declared verification/acceptance MUST equal the implied grade.
rules.error: content class {cls!r} declared {g}-grade but routes to scope {sid!r} whose policy {pol!r} implies {implied}-grade (§8.3b)

rules.precondition: scope_map present
rules.predicate: A BW-ORG publishing a scope_map MUST also declare a member_endpoint (so the scope's member/device set and roster leaves are resolvable cross-provider).
rules.error: BW-ORG publishes a scope_map but no member_endpoint (§8.3a, F14)

rules.precondition: type == BW-MEMBER-v1 AND member_type == 'system'
rules.predicate: A system member MUST carry a mandate_ref (publishing its scoped authority).
rules.error: BW-MEMBER member_type=system without a mandate_ref (Annex R, A2)

rules.precondition: scope_map present; per scope on its recoverability
rules.predicate: recoverability=='records' MUST declare a records_role that is an org-level role and is NOT also one of the scope's own roles; recoverability=='strict' MUST NOT declare a records_role.
rules.error: scope_map.scopes[{i}] recoverability=records requires a records_role (§8.3a, F16) | records_role {rr!r} is not an organisation-level role | records_role {rr!r} is also a scope role (SCOPE-8) | recoverability=strict must not declare a records_role

rules.precondition: type == BW-MEMBER-v1; per device whose capabilities include 'ack' or 'sign'
rules.predicate: An ack/sign-capable device MUST carry a confirmation_key whose public_key_b64 is base64-decodable and whose alg is one of {EdDSA, ES256, ES384}.
rules.error: BW-MEMBER devices[{i}] is ack/sign-capable but has no confirmation_key anchor (finding D) | devices[{i}].confirmation_key.public_key_b64 is not base64-decodable | devices[{i}].confirmation_key.alg {a!r} is not a permitted COSE algorithm

rules.input: BW-MEMBER document (per device carrying an mls_leaf_binding)
rules.precondition: type == BW-MEMBER-v1; a device has an mls_leaf_binding (OPTIONAL in pilot, REQUIRED in production)
rules.predicate: The device's signed binding MUST satisfy: (i) the RFC 9420 rule that the credential key IS the LeafNode signature key — mls_leaf_node_ref.signature_key_hash == SHA-256(mls_leaf_binding.leaf_sig_pubkey_b64); (ii) the binding COSE payload MUST equal dCBOR({uid, mid, device_id, leaf_sig_pubkey_b64}) of THIS device (it binds exactly this device's leaf key to this uid/mid/device_id); and (iii, demo/pilot) when the binding kid is the entity seal signer ('entity-admin'), the COSE signature MUST verify against the entity seal key. The production certificate profile (Basic Constraints/KU/EKU/name constraints/revocation) and the QSealC-chain / Trusted-List validation remain production-verifier duties.
rules.error: BW-MEMBER devices[{i}].mls_leaf_binding.leaf_sig_pubkey_b64 is not base64-decodable | BW-MEMBER devices[{i}]: mls_leaf_node_ref.signature_key_hash != SHA-256(mls_leaf_binding.leaf_sig_pubkey_b64) — the MLS LeafNode signature key is not the bound credential key (RFC 9420) | BW-MEMBER devices[{i}].mls_leaf_binding.binding_cose_b64 is not a decodable COSE_Sign1 | BW-MEMBER devices[{i}] mls_leaf_binding does not bind this device's (uid, mid, device_id, leaf key) — content mismatch | BW-MEMBER devices[{i}] mls_leaf_binding signature does not verify against the entity seal key — the binding was not authorised by the entity (F-04)

rules.precondition: type == BW-ORG-v1
rules.predicate: BW-ORG 2.4: the acceptance_policy map MUST be present, non-empty, and carry the reserved key 'default' — the deterministic selection for entity-addressed default-scope messages (umbrella §8.3), whose eligible set is the ENTIRE active membership. Without it that addressing case selects no policy. Satisfiability of the default key is bundle-level (LINT-BND-07..09, eligible set = all active members).
rules.error: BW-ORG without an acceptance_policy, or without the REQUIRED 'default' key (X-12)

rules.input: STATUS-v1 status-assertion artefact (+ optional directory, optional verification time)
rules.precondition: type == STATUS-v1
rules.predicate: D6: the signed short-lived status capability is well-formed and anchored. STATIC always: validity window non-empty and ≤ the 5-minute suspension-propagation bound (the bound is what makes the concealment window bounded); merged ⇒ redirect_uid; ULID replay guard. With a directory: the seal verifies against a pinned registry_seal_keys entry — only the EDD core registry issues status; an entity's key (even validly pinned for its own documents) cannot. With a verification time: the assertion must be within its validity — outside it an RDP MUST fail closed (umbrella §5.7).
rules.error: empty/overlong validity, merged without redirect, an unanchored or non-verifying registry seal, or reliance outside the validity window (D6)

rules.input: ROSTER-v1 snapshot artefact (+ optional member-doc digests, optional expected tree hash)
rules.precondition: type == ROSTER-v1
rules.predicate: The signed atomic roster snapshot. STATIC always: sealed, non-empty, no duplicate mids. With the entity's sealed BW-MEMBER digests supplied, BOTH directions are enforced — a supplied active member absent from the snapshot is an OMITTED MEMBER (the completeness the signature attests is false); a snapshot digest matching no supplied doc is a MIXED-VERSION enumeration. With the expected ratchet-tree hash (from the retained GroupContext the evidence mls_state commits to), tree_hash must match — enumeration ↔ tree ↔ evidence, one chain. Fail-closed.
rules.error: omitted active member, mixed-version enumeration, duplicate mid, or a tree_hash that does not chain to the evidenced epoch (F-12)

rules.precondition: type == BW-MEMBER-v1 AND two or more devices carry confirmation_key
rules.predicate: One confirmation key per device — two devices of ONE member publishing the same confirmation_key.public_key_b64 collapse device-bound assurance to member-bound and make attribution ambiguous (a signature would verify against both records, including across security classes). Cross-member/cross-entity duplicates are bundle-level (LINT-BND-32). Rollover republishes the SAME device record; a key never moves between devices.
rules.error: two device records of one member publish the same confirmation key (X-32)

rules.input: BW-ORG-v1 document, plus the retrieval/verification instant (--now)
rules.precondition: a `now` is supplied (the check is about what a party retrieving the document at that instant may rely on) and the document carries valid_from
rules.predicate: A BW-ORG served AS CURRENT MUST already be in force — valid_from <= now. The decision settled the open question by PROHIBITING pre-publication rather than adding an `as_of` retrieval API: a relying party fetching the current document cannot tell that a version does not yet bind, and would evaluate an act under rules not yet in force. Parametric on `now` like LINT-DISC-25, because an archived version legitimately has a valid_from in the past of its own service window. Fail-closed on an unparsable instant.
rules.error: BW-ORG served as current takes force at {vf}, AFTER the retrieval time {now} (DR-04/R2-M6)

rules.precondition: the document is a BW-MEMBER (every device record is checked)
rules.predicate: BW-MEMBER 2.2: each device publishes `cipher_suites`, the suites its KeyPackages are served for, and that list MUST contain the mandatory baseline and MUST NOT repeat a suite. The normative selector has always required per-member/device capability sets; nothing published them, so the tests supplied synthetic arrays and the algorithm could not be executed from discovery at all. Requiring the baseline preserves the invariant the selector rests on — the baseline is in every intersection, so a selection always exists — which one device could otherwise break for the whole federation.
rules.error: device publishes no cipher_suites | omits the REQUIRED baseline | repeats a suite (DR-08)

rules.precondition: the device publishes an optional min_cipher_suite
rules.predicate: A device's published floor may only RAISE the mandatory mls-suite-floor/v1, never lower it, and MUST be a suite the device also publishes in cipher_suites. The mandatory floor binds every conforming deployment INCLUDING one that publishes nothing — which is the majority case and exactly where a provider-induced downgrade lands — so this field is a raise and nothing else. A weaker published value is not a weaker policy the federation honours; it is non-conformant, and accepting it would restore the per-participant floor the mandatory floor replaced. Demanding a suite the device cannot use makes every group unformable: a denial of service wearing a policy's clothes.
rules.error: min_cipher_suite is not in the current mls-suite-preference vector (its id, e.g. mls-suite-preference/v2) | is WEAKER than the mandatory floor | is not among the device's own cipher_suites (DR-15)

rules.input: BW-MEMBER-v1 device confirmation_key anchor, under --profile production
rules.precondition: the production profile is selected and the device publishes a confirmation_key
rules.predicate: The anchor MUST carry an `x5chain`, and the LEAF CERTIFICATE MUST HOLD THE SAME PUBLIC KEY as `public_key_b64`, in the encoding the declared `alg` defines (raw Ed25519; SEC1 uncompressed P-256 / P-384). The I-D required this equality and the prose required the chain, but the schema required neither and production lint checked only that some x5chain identity was present on the document SEAL — so a production deployment could publish a bare asserted raw key and the advanced-signature identity claim rested on an assertion. SCOPE: this proves the certificate carries this key; it does NOT validate the chain to a trust anchor, the QSealC qualification, SCD certification or Trusted-List status. Those are the EXTERNAL production trust policy and remain Partial — completing the parsing locally is not completing them.
rules.error: no x5chain in the production profile | the certificate's subject public key is not the published confirmation key | wrong key type or curve for the declared alg (R3-05)

rules.precondition: a BW-PROVIDER-v1 descriptor is validated
rules.predicate: Batch A / A3: the descriptor's validity window MUST run forwards, and where a verification instant is supplied the descriptor MUST be in force at it. Both bounds are parsed to INSTANTS and compared as instants, never as strings — an earlier round closed a defect where a lexically ordered window was chronologically inverted, and a document carrying two timestamps is exactly where that would return.
rules.error: no x5chain in the production profile | the certificate's subject public key is not the published confirmation key | wrong key type or curve for the declared alg (R3-05)

rules.precondition: a BW-PROVIDER-v1 descriptor is validated
rules.predicate: Batch A / A3: every role the descriptor claims MUST be one this version defines. Closed to `rdp` in Batch A, matching the membership register's `role` enum and the descriptor Schema. A role nobody defines is a claim no verifier can act on.
rules.error: no x5chain in the production profile | the certificate's subject public key is not the published confirmation key | wrong key type or curve for the declared alg (R3-05)

rules.precondition: --profile production; cbor2 available and doc_cose_b64 valid; protected header decodes
rules.predicate: The production discovery seal's COSE protected header MUST embed a verifier-resolvable QSealC identity — label 33 (x5chain) or 34 (x5t).
rules.error: production discovery seal must embed a verifier-resolvable QSealC identity (COSE x5chain/x5t)

rules.precondition: --profile production; protected header decodes
rules.predicate: The seal's COSE kid MUST NOT equal 'rdp' — discovery documents are entity-published, not sealed by the RDP evidence signer.
rules.error: discovery document sealed by the RDP evidence signer; discovery documents are entity-published (signer-type mismatch)

rules.precondition: --profile production; protected header decodes
rules.predicate: The seal's COSE kid MUST NOT be a demo kid {rdp, entity-admin, wallet, demo} (rdp handled by P-02); and the document JSON MUST NOT contain any demo/example URL marker {example.eu, example.fr, example.com, example.org}.
rules.error: demo COSE kid {kid!r} in production discovery document | demo/example URL ({m}) in production discovery document

rules.precondition: type == EP-v1
rules.predicate: se.message_id MUST equal ep.message_id, and every outcomes[i].message_id MUST equal ep.message_id.
rules.error: se.message_id != EP message_id | outcomes[{i}].message_id != EP message_id

rules.precondition: type == EP-v1
rules.predicate: The set of rdp_ids referenced by se.rdp_id and each outcomes[].rdp_id MUST be fully covered by the rdp_ids present in rdp_chain.
rules.error: rdp_chain does not cover rdp_ids {missing}

rules.precondition: type == EP-v1
rules.predicate: ep.seal MUST contain a 'qualified_timestamp' key.
rules.error: EP seal missing qualified_timestamp

rules.precondition: type == EP-v1, per states[i]
rules.predicate: Each state record's keys MUST be a subset of {state, event, at, mid, device_id}; no other fields.
rules.error: states[{i}] has non-state-record fields {extra} (state records establish no delivery and carry no Article 43(2) effect)

rules.precondition: type == EP-v1, per outcomes[i] whose scope_ref is not None
rules.predicate: outcomes[i].scope_ref MUST equal se.scope_ref (all outcomes share the enclosed SE's confidentiality scope).
rules.error: outcomes[{i}].scope_ref {a!r} != se.scope_ref {b!r}

rules.precondition: type == EP-v1, per rdp_chain[i] whose `evidence` is a dict
rules.predicate: evidence.message_id MUST equal ep.message_id; evidence.event MUST be in {B.1-RelayAcceptance, B.2-RelayRejection}; evidence.seal_digest.hex MUST be 64 lowercase-hex chars.
rules.error: rdp_chain[{i}].evidence.message_id {a!r} != EP message_id {b!r} | rdp_chain[{i}].evidence.event {e!r} is not a B.x relay event | rdp_chain[{i}].evidence.seal_digest.hex is not lowercase 64-hex

rules.precondition: type == EP-v1
rules.predicate: The number of outcomes whose type is in {DE-v1, NDE-v1, RE-v1} (terminal outcomes) MUST be at most 1.
rules.error: EP carries {n} terminal outcomes {kinds} for one message — at most one is allowed (finding R4)

rules.precondition: type == EP-v1 AND changes[] or disputes[] present
rules.predicate: Every nested change (CE) and dispute (GCM) binds THIS package's message — its message_id MUST equal the EP's. Outcomes and the SE were already bound; changes were unchecked, and the shipped federated fixture carried a foreign message's CE. A package never carries another message's evidence.
rules.error: a nested change/dispute whose message_id differs from the EP's (X-31)

rules.input: GCM-v1 evidence object (standalone or in an EP's disputes[])
rules.precondition: type == GCM-v1
rules.predicate: D5 (evidence 2.2): the grade-commitment-mismatch dispute object is structurally coherent — the reveal carries a hex salt and a content_class; within an EP the GCM's message_id MUST equal the SE's and its grade_commitment MUST echo the SE's sealed commitment (the dispute references the disputed value). The declared-grade verification against the pinned ORG is bundle-level (LINT-BND-26). A GCM is rebuttal-only supplementary evidence: it never retracts the DE and is not a terminal outcome. With the SE, the `reveal_confirmation` itself must name the SE's `message_id`, `recipient_uid`, `envelope_hash` and `grade_commitment` (`evidence_lint.reveal_binding`) — the rule the issuing path applies before a reveal is recorded.
rules.error: GCM reveal missing or malformed (salt, content_class) | GCM reveal.salt is not hex | GCM message_id != se.message_id | GCM grade_commitment does not echo the SE's sealed commitment — the dispute must reference the disputed value

rules.precondition: type == GCM-v1
rules.predicate: The dispute's own coherence, as TYPED violations rather than exceptions — the top-level mid equals auth_context.mid; envelope_hash is present (a dispute binds to the disputed OCTETS, not merely to a message_id); reveal.salt is exactly 32 lowercase hex characters (16 bytes — the former schema admitted 1..64 bytes AND odd lengths, and an odd-length salt raised an uncaught ValueError inside the cross-document validator); the reveal_confirmation's wallet signature binds to its own canonical content.
rules.error: mid/auth_context.mid disagreement, missing envelope_hash, or a salt that is not exactly 16 bytes (DR-03)

rules.input: the whole evidence or discovery document (recursively)
rules.precondition: always — every object carrying a `hash_mode` member, wherever it sits: `payload_hash`, the envelope `content_digest`, `acceptance_policy_ref.doc_digest`, a manifest part descriptor
rules.predicate: Every `hash_mode` MUST be one the profile defines: raw-sha256, raw-sha512, manifest-sha256, manifest-sha512. A digest is always over octets — `raw-*` over the transmitted bytes (Mode A), `manifest-*` over the deterministic-CBOR manifest whose part digests are over each part's own octets (Mode C). The JSON-canonicalisation modes jcs-sha256 and jcs-sha512 were REMOVED on 2026-09-25 and are refused by name: a verifier meeting one cannot recompute the digest, so accepting the artefact would assert a check that was never made.
rules.error: hash_mode {mode!r} at {path} is not part of the profile — removed 2026-09-25; JSON canonicalisation left the profile; the profile defines raw-sha256, raw-sha512, manifest-sha256, manifest-sha512

rules.precondition: SE has a `manifest` list
rules.predicate: All part_id values within the manifest MUST be unique.
rules.error: duplicate part_id in manifest

rules.precondition: SE has a `manifest` list
rules.predicate: The sequence of part_id values MUST already be in byte-wise ascending (sorted) order.
rules.error: manifest is not in byte-wise ascending part_id order

rules.input: any evidence object carrying a `manifest` (SE, or an EP sub-object)
rules.precondition: a `manifest` list is present and non-empty
rules.predicate: `payload_hash.hash_mode` MUST be a manifest-* mode, and `payload_hash.hex` MUST equal SHA-256 (or SHA-512, per `alg`) over the deterministic-CBOR encoding of the manifest the object carries — a list of maps, each with the full hash descriptor, as cddl/sm-mls-erd.cddl defines it. This is the half of the multipart binding that a party WITHOUT the plaintext can verify; that each part carries the digest of its own octets cannot be verified from evidence, the parts being end-to-end encrypted and absent, and the two claims must not be conflated.
rules.error: payload_hash {declared} is not the digest of the manifest present ({computed}) — SHA-256/512 over the deterministic-CBOR encoding of the manifest, a list of maps per the CDDL

rules.precondition: type == NDE-v1 AND reason == 'payload-hash-mismatch'
rules.predicate: recipient_confirmation.result MUST equal 'mismatch'.
rules.error: reason=payload-hash-mismatch requires recipient_confirmation.result == 'mismatch'

rules.precondition: type == NDE-v1 AND reason == 'uid-merged'
rules.predicate: redirect_uid MUST be a well-formed EU UID (UID_RE).
rules.error: reason=uid-merged requires a well-formed redirect_uid

rules.precondition: type == NDE-v1 AND reason == 'payload-hash-mismatch'
rules.predicate: recipient_confirmation.message_id MUST equal nde.message_id.
rules.error: recipient_confirmation.message_id != NDE message_id

rules.input: NDE evidence object with enclosing SE context
rules.precondition: type == NDE-v1 AND reason == 'payload-hash-mismatch' AND an SE context is supplied
rules.predicate: recipient_confirmation.mls_group_id MUST equal se.mls_group_id AND recipient_confirmation.mls_epoch MUST equal se.mls_epoch. The proof's `mls_state` must equal the SE's as well — the confirmation carries it, and the S3 arm already bound it (LINT-DE-16); the issuing path runs this rule before an NDE is sealed.
rules.error: recipient_confirmation MLS session != se.mls_group_id/mls_epoch

rules.input: NDE evidence object with enclosing SE context
rules.precondition: type == NDE-v1 AND reason == 'payload-hash-mismatch' AND an SE context is supplied
rules.predicate: recipient_confirmation.acceptance_policy_ref MUST equal se.acceptance_policy_ref.
rules.error: recipient_confirmation.acceptance_policy_ref != se.acceptance_policy_ref

rules.precondition: type == NDE-v1 AND reason == 'payload-hash-mismatch'
rules.predicate: recipient_confirmation.payload_hash MUST DIFFER from nde.payload_hash (equality would contradict the mismatch claim).
rules.error: recipient_confirmation.payload_hash must differ from the NDE (sender) payload_hash

rules.precondition: type == NDE-v1 AND reason has a defined event mapping
rules.predicate: nde.event MUST be in the allowed EN 319 522-1 event set REGISTERED for that reason in registries/reason-codes.json (the reason->event binding table is loaded from the machine-readable registry artefact owned by the design authority, umbrella §13.4 — registering or re-binding a code is a registry action, not a lint-code change). A reason with no registered binding (allowed_events null, or unregistered) is skipped here; unregistered codes are LINT-NDE-W1's concern.
rules.error: reason {reason!r} requires event in {allowed}, got {ev!r}

rules.input: NDE evidence object (+ its SE where available)
rules.precondition: type == NDE-v1 AND reason == 'payload-validation-failed'
rules.predicate: The NDE carries a recipient_validation_failure and NOT a recipient_confirmation; its `failure`, and each entry in `parts[]`, is a registered cause. INTRINSIC, checked whether or not the SE is available, because each is decidable from the assertion alone (R27-PUB-03): every part carries the fields its cause requires and none it forbids — a digest mismatch carries BOTH `declared` and `observed`, an absent or undescribed part carries no `observed` digest and an undescribed part quotes no declaration the sender never made; a claimed digest mismatch's two digests DIFFER and lie in the SAME digest domain (same alg and hash_mode, since digests in different domains are unequal whatever the octets were); a claimed digest mismatch does not carry differing lengths, which would make it a part-length-mismatch, the more precise cause; and a claimed length mismatch carries both lengths and they differ. SE-DEPENDENT, checked only where the SE is available: each part is described by the manifest (or claimed undescribed and absent from it), the quoted `declared` and `declared_length` are what the sender actually declared, the assertion's declared_payload_hash equals se.payload_hash, and its mls_group_id / mls_epoch / mls_state / acceptance_policy_ref equal the SE's. The intrinsic checks used to sit behind the SE-availability branch, so an assertion verified from retained evidence alone was never examined.
rules.error: the recipient validation failure does not bind to the message it is about, or asserts a comparison it did not make, or contradicts itself

rules.precondition: type == NDE-v1 AND reason is a well-formed lowercase-kebab token NOT present in registries/reason-codes.json
rules.predicate: Safe generic processing: a well-formed but UNREGISTERED reason code is accepted structurally, preserved verbatim and treated as a generic non-delivery. This rule emits a WARNING (the -W convention: printed, never counted as a violation) so an additive registration is safe for an older verifier — the I-D's unknown-code ingest rule, made implementable. A REGISTERED reason still enforces its event binding via LINT-NDE-07.
rules.error: reason {reason!r} is not a REGISTERED reason code — accepted and preserved verbatim; treat as a generic non-delivery (registries/reason-codes.json; the I-D, IANA Considerations)

rules.precondition: type in {SE-v1,DE-v1,NDE-v1,RE-v1,CE-v1}
rules.predicate: obj.seal MUST be an object; seal.cose_b64 MUST be valid Base64, decode to CBOR, and be a 4-element COSE_Sign1 array. (Structural CBOR checks require cbor2.)
rules.error: seal container missing or not an object | {field} is not valid Base64 | {field} does not decode to CBOR | {field} is not a 4-element COSE_Sign1 array

rules.precondition: type == EP-v1
rules.predicate: ep.seal MUST be an object; seal.cose_b64 MUST be valid Base64, decode to CBOR, and be a 4-element COSE_Sign1 array.
rules.error: seal container missing or not an object | {field} is not valid Base64 | {field} does not decode to CBOR | {field} is not a 4-element COSE_Sign1 array

rules.precondition: any evidence object with a seal
rules.predicate: seal.qualified_timestamp.token_b64 MUST be valid Base64 AND decode to a non-empty byte string whose first byte is 0x30 (a DER SEQUENCE).
rules.error: qualified_timestamp.token_b64 is not valid Base64 | qualified_timestamp.token_b64 does not decode to a DER SEQUENCE (leading 0x30)

rules.input: any COSE_Sign1: a seal.cose_b64 or a confirmation's wallet_signature_b64
rules.precondition: a seal (any evidence object) or a confirmation carrying wallet_signature_b64; cbor2 required
rules.predicate: The COSE protected header MUST decode to CBOR and its alg (label 1) MUST be in the allowlist {EdDSA(-8), ES256(-7), ES384(-35)}; a wallet_signature_b64 MUST be valid Base64, decode to CBOR, and be a 4-element COSE_Sign1.
rules.error: {field} protected header is not decodable CBOR | {field} COSE alg {alg!r} not in allowlist | {field} is not valid Base64 | {field} does not decode to CBOR | {field} is not a 4-element COSE_Sign1 array

rules.input: a sealed object + its seal.cose_b64, or a confirmation + its wallet_signature_b64
rules.precondition: cbor2 available AND the COSE b64 is valid Base64 (else deferred to LINT-PKG-01/02)
rules.predicate: The COSE_Sign1 payload MUST be embedded bytes (not detached) and MUST byte-for-byte equal the deterministic-CBOR (dCBOR) encoding of the reconstructed signed payload: for an EP, dcbor(ep_signed_body) with sub-objects embedded as artefact bytes; otherwise dcbor(obj minus the strip field(s) — 'seal', or 'wallet_signature_b64' for a confirmation).
rules.error: {label} COSE payload is detached (not embedded) | {label} COSE payload does not match the object's canonical signed payload (stale or tampered evidence)

rules.precondition: cose_b64 and token_b64 valid Base64 AND the token is in the demo/mock format (len==36, first 4 bytes 0x30 0x22 0x04 0x20)
rules.predicate: The token's 32-byte message imprint (bytes[4:]) MUST equal SHA-256 of the decoded inner-COSE bytes (SHA-256(b64decode(cose_b64))).
rules.error: {label} qualified_timestamp imprint != SHA-256(seal)

rules.input: the whole evidence or discovery document (recursively)
rules.precondition: always
rules.predicate: No JSON number anywhere may be a float, and no integer may exceed |2^53-1| (9007199254740991); bool is ignored (I-JSON: integers only; carry large counters as decimal strings).
rules.error: floating-point number (I-JSON: integers only) at {p} | integer {n} outside the safe range +/-(2^53-1) at {p}

rules.input: the raw JSON file text (evidence or discovery)
rules.precondition: always — enforced at parse time (strict loader)
rules.predicate: No JSON object may contain a duplicate key; a duplicate is rejected and the file failed.
rules.error: [FAIL] {f}: LINT-PKG-10 duplicate object key(s): {sorted keys}

rules.input: any wrapped artefact {sm_artifact_b64, projection} (evidence, discovery, or an EP with wrapped sub-artefacts)
rules.precondition: the input is a dict carrying both 'sm_artifact_b64' and 'projection' (non-wrapped input passes silently)
rules.predicate: The wire `projection` MUST equal decode(payload) EXACTLY under recursive structural equality: dicts by key-SET (order-independent) recursing each shared key, lists by length AND positional order, scalars by type-and-value, and a bool NEVER equal to an int. The authoritative payload is decoded from sm_artifact_b64 (discovery: COSE_Sign1 payload of the raw bytes; evidence: dcbor([cose,qts]) then the COSE payload). For an EP the comparison is de-zipped: non-sub keys must match; `se` presence must match and its projection compared to the decoded sub-artefact; `outcomes` and `changes` MUST have equal length and each element compared by decoding its sub-artefact bytes. Any decode failure fails closed.
rules.error: cannot decode the authoritative payload: {exc} | {path}.{k} present on only one side | {path}.{k} differs between projection and payload | {path}.se present on only one side | {path}.{k}: projection carries {n} element(s), the signed payload carries {m} | {path}: projection differs from decode(payload)

rules.input: any wrapped artefact {sm_artifact_b64, projection} (evidence or discovery)
rules.precondition: the input is a dict carrying both 'sm_artifact_b64' and 'projection' (the linters' ingest path; also run per-sample by the cddl-check gate)
rules.predicate: N-02: the decoded body MUST validate against its AUTHORITATIVE JSON Schema (resolved from the body's `type` via the type->schema map; Draft 2020-12, format-asserting, local $ref store). The CDDL is only the structural outer bound, so a body that is CDDL-valid and projection-equal but Schema-invalid — e.g. a minimal {type, version} discovery body — is rejected fail-closed at the verifier entry point.
rules.error: decoded body does not validate against its authoritative JSON Schema ({schema_file}): {path}: {message} (+{n} more)

rules.input: a production evidence seal.cose_b64 (and each confirmation's wallet_signature_b64)
rules.precondition: profile == 'production' AND type in EVIDENCE_DOC_TYPES; cbor2 available and COSE b64 valid
rules.predicate: The COSE protected header MUST embed a verifier-resolvable QSealC identity — x5chain (label 33) or x5t (label 34).
rules.error: {label}: production seal must embed a verifier-resolvable QSealC identity (COSE x5chain/x5t)

rules.precondition: profile == 'production' AND qualified_timestamp is a dict
rules.predicate: qualified_timestamp.tsa_id MUST be present and truthy.
rules.error: production qualified_timestamp must carry a tsa_id

rules.input: a production evidence object (COSE kid, profile, tsa_id, rdp_id, policy_id; nested EP sub-objects/wallet sigs)
rules.precondition: profile == 'production' AND type in EVIDENCE_DOC_TYPES
rules.predicate: The COSE kid (label 4) MUST NOT be a demo kid (b'rdp'/b'wallet'); a present `profile` field MUST equal 'production'; tsa_id MUST NOT contain a demo marker (example.eu/MockEU/example.); rdp_id and policy_id MUST NOT contain a demo marker.
rules.error: {label}: demo COSE kid {kid!r} in production evidence | profile is {p!r}, not 'production' | tsa_id contains a demo marker: {v} | {f} contains a demo marker: {v}

rules.precondition: type == RE-v1
rules.predicate: Evidence 2.3: kind/reason/proof coherence. refusal_kind 'member' claims a user act: reason MUST be 'refused-by-user' and a recipient-produced refusal_confirmation MUST be present with mid/message_id/payload_hash matching the RE — an RDP-only assertion of a user act is rejected. refusal_kind 'organisation-policy' claims no user act: it MUST NOT carry a member-kind reason (per the registry refusal_kind binding), a refusing mid, or a refusal_confirmation.
rules.error: member refusal without member proof, mismatched refusal_confirmation content, or a policy refusal claiming a user act (X-29)

rules.precondition: type == RelayEvidence-v1
rules.predicate: If event == 'B.2-RelayRejection', reason MUST be one of {malformed, policy-violation, uid-suspended, unknown-uid}; if event == 'B.1-RelayAcceptance', reason MUST be absent.
rules.error: B.2-RelayRejection reason {r!r} is not a typed relay-rejection reason {set} | B.1-RelayAcceptance must not carry a rejection reason

rules.precondition: type == RelayEvidence-v1
rules.predicate: sending_rdp_id and receiving_rdp_id MUST both be present and MUST NOT be equal (a relay hop is between two distinct providers).
rules.error: relay evidence must name both sending_rdp_id and receiving_rdp_id | sending_rdp_id == receiving_rdp_id ({s!r}) — a relay hop is between two distinct providers

rules.input: any evidence or discovery object + its seal + the loaded trust store
rules.precondition: a trust store was supplied (--trust-store)
rules.predicate: The seal MUST decode as a COSE_Sign1; its kid (protected-header label 4) MUST resolve to a store entry; and the Ed25519 signature over ['Signature1', protected, b'', payload] MUST verify against that entry's pubkey_b64. Fail-closed (the signature step is skipped only if the signing library is unimportable).
rules.error: seal is not a decodable COSE_Sign1 — cannot resolve a signer against the trust store (fail-closed) | seal kid {kid!r} does not resolve to a trust-store entry (fail-closed: unknown signer) | seal signature does not verify against the trust-store key for kid {kid!r}

rules.input: any evidence or discovery object + resolved trust-store entry + signer identity
rules.precondition: a trust store was supplied AND the seal kid resolved to an entry
rules.predicate: The entry's role MUST equal the expected role for the family ('evidence-rdp' for evidence, 'discovery-publisher' for discovery); and if a signer identity (rdp_id for SE/DE/NDE/RE/CE, receiving_rdp_id for RelayEvidence, se.rdp_id for EP, uid for discovery) is supplied and the entry declares identities, that identity MUST be among them.
rules.error: kid {kid!r} has store role {role!r}, expected {expected!r} for this document type | signer identity {id!r} is not among the trust-store identities for kid {kid!r}

rules.input: any evidence or discovery object + resolved trust-store entry
rules.precondition: a trust store was supplied, the kid resolved, AND the object declares at least one instant
rules.predicate: The object's latest declared RFC 3339 Zulu instant (issuance-style keys: at/valid_from/last_seen/timestamp or *_at except expires_at) MUST lie within [entry.not_before, entry.not_after] by string comparison (no wall clock).
rules.error: object instant {inst} lies outside the trust-store validity window [{nb}, {na}] for kid {kid!r}

rules.input: RelayEvidence-v1 object + the loaded trust store
rules.precondition: a trust store was supplied AND type == RelayEvidence-v1 AND sending_rdp_id present AND the known evidence-rdp identity set is non-empty
rules.predicate: The relaying peer named in sending_rdp_id MUST resolve to a known evidence-rdp identity — the union of identities across all store entries whose role == 'evidence-rdp'.
rules.error: relay sending_rdp_id {peer!r} does not resolve to a known evidence-rdp identity in the trust store {known} — FC-3 peer authentication

rules.input: any discovery document + its seal + the trust store + the directory-pin fixture (--trust-store + --directory)
rules.precondition: a trust store AND a directory fixture were supplied
rules.predicate: The discovery seal's signing key (resolved from the COSE kid via the store) MUST be an authorized seal key pinned by the directory for THIS document's UID: its spki_sha256 (SHA-256 of the raw seal public key; production pins the QSealC x5t#S256) MUST appear in DirectoryRecord.authorized_seal_keys for the document's uid, and the object's latest instant MUST lie within that pinned key's window. A key not pinned for this UID — including a valid QSealC authorised for another UID — is rejected fail-closed; a UID with no directory pin is rejected fail-closed. (Pilot/demo scope; the production QSealC-chain / Trusted-List validation is a production-verifier duty.)
rules.error: no directory record pins an authorized seal key for UID {uid!r} (fail-closed: unbound discovery-seal authority) | discovery seal key (spki-sha256 …) is not an authorized seal key for UID {uid!r} in the directory record (a key authorised for another UID cannot seal here) | discovery seal key for UID {uid!r} is pinned but the object instant {inst} lies outside its authorised key-set window (rotation/retirement)

rules.input: a loaded bundle + the federation membership register (manifest `federation_register`)
rules.precondition: a federation register was supplied; its ABSENCE is the declared `federation-admission` gap, reported INCOMPLETE by the required-property registry rather than by this rule
rules.predicate: For every provider identifier the bundle's evidence names — the set of fields DERIVED from the evidence Schemas by `rdp_identity_inventory`, so `rdp_id`, relay's `sending_rdp_id`/`receiving_rdp_id` and each EP `rdp_chain[]` entry are covered without a hand-written list — the register MUST attribute status `admitted` to that participant AT THE INSTANT OF ITS OWN ACT (`sent_at`, `delivered_at`, `observed_at`, `refused_at`, `changed_at`, `read_at`, `hop_at`, or the chain entry's own `timestamp`), resolved over half-open `[from, until)` windows and compared as INSTANTS (umbrella §13.1; `lint_cli.admission_at`). `suspended`, `excluded`, no status at that instant, a register that cannot answer, and a provider whose act this verifier cannot date are each a violation. Admission is NOT qualification: this establishes no Trusted-List status. A record is relied on only for acts at or before its `asserted_at`; for a later act it establishes nothing, and that act is reported as the `federation-admission` gap (LINT-BND-I6), never as admitted and never as a violation. An Evidence Package's COMPOSER (se.rdp_id) is resolved at the instant the package's own qualified timestamp attests — composition is an act, distinct from the acts the package records; a timestamp with no readable instant leaves it unestablished (LINT-BND-I6).
rules.error: {type} {where} names provider {pid!r}, which the register records as {status!r} at {at}, the instant of the act itself | … to which the register attributes no status at {at} — the provider is unknown to the federation, or acted before it was admitted | … but no act instant is in scope for it, so admission cannot be evaluated at the moment of the act | … the register cannot answer for {pid!r} at {at}: {exc}

rules.input: a BW-PROVIDER-v1 descriptor + its seal + the trust store + the federation membership register (--trust-store + --federation-register)
rules.precondition: a trust store AND a federation register were supplied AND the document is a BW-PROVIDER-v1
rules.predicate: `LINT-TRUST-05` one level up. The descriptor's signing key (resolved from the COSE kid via the store) MUST be an authorized seal key pinned by the participant's `MembershipRecord` — its `spki_sha256` MUST appear in `authorized_seal_keys`, and the descriptor's `asserted_at` MUST fall within that pinned key's own `[not_before, not_after]` window — AND the register MUST attribute status `admitted` to the participant at that same `asserted_at`. A participant with no record is rejected fail-closed. One rule because both arms answer one question: does the register authorise THIS descriptor? Instants, never strings. (Pilot/demo scope; the production QSealC-chain / Trusted-List validation is a production-verifier duty.) A register record asserted BEFORE the descriptor cannot speak for the descriptor's instant; with no third verdict in this linter, that fails closed.
rules.error: no membership record pins an authorized seal key for participant {pid!r} (fail-closed: a descriptor nobody in the federation vouches for) | descriptor seal key (spki-sha256 …) is not an authorized seal key for participant {pid!r} in the membership register | descriptor seal key for participant {pid!r} is pinned but the descriptor is asserted at {asserted}, outside the pinned key's window (rotation / retirement) | the register attributes status {status!r} / NO status to participant {pid!r} at {asserted}, so it does not authorise this descriptor | the register's record for {pid!r} was asserted before the descriptor ({asserted}), so it cannot speak for the instant the descriptor asserts itself

rules.input: a federation membership register + the configured Federation Authority anchors (every trust-store entry whose role is `federation-authority`, keyed by kid)
rules.precondition: a membership register was supplied to a check that would consult it (bundle admission, LINT-TRUST-06; descriptor pinning, LINT-TRUST-07)
rules.predicate: The register is authenticated AT INGRESS, before any status or pinned key in it is read, against an anchor that is configuration and never part of the input. Every record MUST carry a seal and a timestamp; the seal MUST be a COSE_Sign1 whose kid names a configured Federation Authority anchor (an anchor SET, so the authority can rotate its key: each record is verified under the key its own kid names); its payload MUST equal the deterministic CBOR of the record minus {signature, timestamp}; the signature MUST verify under the anchor's key; that anchor MUST be valid at the record's asserted_at — a retired key does not keep speaking; the timestamp MUST imprint SHA-256 of the seal (demo token; full RFC 3161 validation is the production verifier's); the record MUST validate against MembershipRecord; its status_history MUST be well-formed; and the register MUST carry one record per participant. All or nothing: one failing record means the register is not consulted at all. A register supplied with no anchor configured is not authenticated and not consulted.
rules.error: membership record {i} ({pid!r}) carries no seal/timestamp | …is sealed under kid {kid!r}, not the configured Federation Authority | …differs from what its seal signed — a field was changed after sealing | …seal does not verify under the Federation Authority's key | …asserted outside the anchor's validity window | …timestamp does not imprint SHA-256 of the seal | …is not a valid MembershipRecord | …{history reason} | the register carries N records for {pid!r} | no Federation Authority anchor is configured | a register was supplied with no trust store

rules.input: a seal.cose_b64, or a confirmation's wallet_signature_b64
rules.precondition: --verify-demo mode; cbor2 and pynacl available and COSE b64 valid
rules.predicate: The COSE_Sign1 Ed25519 signature over ['Signature1', protected, b'', payload] MUST verify against the published demo public key ('demo' for object seals, 'wallet-demo' for wallet signatures).
rules.error: {label}: COSE signature does not verify against the demo {seed!r} key
